text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hariri refuses to include opposition politicians in his government.
-Russian Foreign Minister Primakov met the head of the socialist party Jumblatt before leaving Beirut to Cairo.
-Greenpeace Lebanon representative Hamdan: Germany is legally and morally responsible for the 36 containers of toxic waste and will take them back within the coming few days.
-Hariri did not set a date for forming the cabinet: We are still studying the possibilities.
-The constitutional council to meet on Saturday to mull appeals by losers in parliamentary elections.
-Societe des grands hotels du liban, the Lebanese company rebuilding two of Beirut grand hotels to list its shares on the bourse.
-Israeli shelling of the Iqlim al-Toufah mountain ridges and mock air raids over the south. Israeli troops and their local allies detained a number of citizens inside the zone including women.
-Austrian economic delegation in Beirut said Austria was interested in cooperating with both private and public sectors.
-House Speaker Berri told several deputies that some Lebanese political parties have secret contacts with Israel.
-President Hrawi, House Speaker Berri and Hariri expected to meet today.
